findings.title: Bare-plural/singular query mismatch silently kills concept matching for a large share of vocabulary (systemic, not a one-off)
findings.repro: interpretQuery/searchWithRelaxation/classifyResults on paired queries: satellite vs satellites, astronaut vs astronauts, drone vs drones, algorithm vs algorithms, transistor vs transistors, entrepreneur vs entrepreneurs, fusion vs fusions, energy vs energies, culture vs cultures, computer vs computers, soldier vs soldiers, gladiator vs gladiators, recipe vs recipes
findings.evidence: classifyResults output for each pair (script rt_plural_scale.js, run against real data/discover.json + data/semantic-index.json): satellite status=empty picks=0 | satellites status=ok picks=10; astronaut status=empty picks=0 | astronauts status=ok picks=10; drone status=empty picks=0 | drones status=ok picks=10; algorithm status=empty picks=0 | algorithms status=ok picks=10; transistor status=empty picks=0 | transistors status=ok picks=7; entrepreneur status=empty picks=0 | entrepreneurs status=ok picks=10; fusion status=ok picks=10 | fusions status=empty picks=0; energy status=ok picks=10 | energies status=empty picks=0; culture status=ok picks=10 | cultures status=empty picks=0; computer status=sparse picks=3 | computers status=ok picks=10; soldier status=sparse picks=3 | soldiers status=ok picks=10; gladiator status=empty picks=0 | gladiators status=ok picks=8; recipe status=sparse picks=3 | recipes status=ok picks=10. Root cause: semantic-index.json concepts[cid].terms lists only ONE of {singular, plural} per lemma for most concepts (measured: of 1364 total concept terms, 305 have a plural-present/singular-absent gap; 848 are singular-only with no plural counterpart present). A token missing its concept's exact listed inflection gets hasConceptExpansion=false, and if corpusDF is also under THIN_ANCHOR_DF (0.002) it is classified thin=true, so the THIN ANCHOR gate then requires it to literally text-match a result on its own -- LONG_INFLECTIONS only covers inflection variance in matched TEXT, not query-side vocabulary lookup. This is a distinct, much larger-blast-radius instance of the thin-anchor failure class than the already-fixed #209 Electrical Circuit Design Dummies case.

findings.title: Single-word show-name query in the topic search box returns empty even when the show has many episodes in the pool (show-name rescue never fires for 1-token queries)
findings.repro: interpretQuery(q)/searchWithRelaxation()/classifyResults() for one-word show names typed as topic-box queries: volts, radiolab, gastropod, spycast, causality, storycorps, lingthusiasm, palaeocast, foundmyfitness, unexplainable, acquired
findings.evidence: rt_oneword_shows.js output against real data/discover.json (poolCount = actual episode count for that show in the pool): Acquired poolCount=8 status=empty picks=0; Gastropod poolCount=9 status=empty picks=0; Lingthusiasm poolCount=3 status=empty picks=0; SpyCast poolCount=9 status=empty picks=0; Causality poolCount=2 status=empty picks=0; Volts poolCount=12 status=empty picks=0; Radiolab poolCount=8 status=empty picks=0; Unexplainable poolCount=13 status=empty picks=0; Palaeocast poolCount=4 status=empty picks=0; FoundMyFitness poolCount=3 status=empty picks=0; StoryCorps poolCount=7 status=empty picks=0 -- 11 of 23 one-word shows tested return a flat empty with real episodes sitting in the pool. Root cause confirmed by direct scoreMatch trace: querying volts against a real Volts episode scores sum=1.35 matched=0 (show-field hit alone only contributes f += 1, never reaching the 1.2 per-group qualifying bar), and the full-phrase show-name RESCUE (search-engine.js L831-861, +8 to sum when every query token appears in the show name) is gated interp.groups.length >= 2 -- confirmed directly: radiolab groups.length=1 -> rescue eligible? false for every one-word case tested.

findings.title: Boundary case just above THIN_ANCHOR_DF with no concept coverage still degrades when combined with a broad word, though the honesty floor mostly saves it
findings.repro: interpretQuery('Ornithology History Explained', ctx) / interpretQuery('Ornithology Science Basics', ctx)
findings.evidence: ornithology has corpusDF=0.0021, just above THIN_ANCHOR_DF (0.002) and has no concept expansion, so thin=false and the thin-anchor gate does NOT protect it. Ornithology History Explained -> status=sparse, top result 'Strigiformology (OWLS) Part 1...' sum=3.38 matched=1/2 (only the broad history token matched -- ornithology itself contributed 0 to that pick despite being the query's actual subject), all 4 sparse picks share this shape. classifyResults' honesty floor kept the status at sparse (not a dishonest ok/rich padded set), so this is not user-facing-broken today, but it demonstrates THIN_ANCHOR_DF=0.002 has a live, non-hypothetical boundary case immediately above it (0.0021) with materially thinner margin than the code comment implies.

areas_clean: Word-order sensitivity: bag-of-words scorer is fully order-insensitive as designed; verified 'startup founders' vs 'founders startup', 'nuclear energy fusion' vs 'energy fusion nuclear', 'crime junkie' vs 'junkie crime' produce byte-identical result sets/scores.
ALIASES map (bbq/barbeque, rome, ww2, car/cars, ocean, plane/planes, cooking): all produce sensible, on-topic top results; no misfires found.

Honest sparse/empty behavior for genuinely obscure real topics (bagpipes, macrame, blacksmithing, competitive chess, underwater basket weaving): all correctly return classifyStatus=empty with zero picks rather than padding with off-topic filler.
Stage-2 show-name search (SearchEngine.searchShows over data/catalog.json) vs topic search boundary: cleanly separated code paths; no leakage found between the two search modes in either direction.

Backend breadth show-name search (backend/src/catalog/searchBreadthShows.ts + api/shows/search.ts): documented duplicate of the same three-rank substring matcher as searchShows; degrades to empty-with-degraded:true on catalogue read failure rather than 500ing. No divergence found.

The already-fixed #209 Electrical Circuit Design Dummies bug class stays fixed for every new instance of that exact shape constructed (15 distinct thin-hobby-noun + broad-word combinations) -- all honestly return classifyStatus=empty rather than being carried by the broad word alone.
